questions.category: A1 — Use codes, regulations and standards
questions.question: A millwright is asked to install a guard on a machine. Which document should be checked first for minimum legal guarding requirements?
questions.explanation: Legal safety requirements come from occupational health and safety regulations. Manufacturer instructions may add detail, but regulations set minimum requirements. Machine guarding must meet both legal and workplace standards.

questions.category: A2 — Use PPE and safety equipment
questions.question: A worker is using compressed air to clean chips from a part. What is the greatest concern?
options: The air may cool the part
questions.explanation: Compressed air can launch metal chips into eyes or skin. Eye and face protection are required where flying particles exist. Many workplaces restrict compressed air use for cleaning.

questions.question: A temporary extension cord must cross a walkway. What is the best control?
options: Cover or reroute it to prevent tripping and damage
Tell workers to step over it
Leave it loose because it is temporary
questions.explanation: Cords across walkways create trip hazards. They may also be damaged by foot or equipment traffic. Routing or protecting cords controls both hazards.

questions.category: A4 — Lock-out, tag-out and zero energy procedures
questions.question: Which energy source is most likely overlooked during lockout of a pneumatic machine?
options: Stored compressed air in lines or cylinders
questions.explanation: Pneumatic systems may retain pressure after supply isolation. Stored air can move cylinders unexpectedly. Zero energy requires bleeding or controlling stored pressure.

questions.category: B1 — Use hand and portable power tools
questions.question: A torque wrench clicks before reaching the specified torque. What is the most likely issue?
options: The wrench may be set incorrectly or already loaded
questions.explanation: Torque wrenches must be set and used correctly. Preloaded or improperly reset wrenches give inaccurate results. Incorrect torque can cause fastener failure or loosening.
